scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance window, routes for 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8,
and 90.0.0.0/8 became less stable in r1's RIB. r3 reports
losing an OSPF neighbor. Find the affected link.

injection.action: bring down the link toward r9

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r3 link toward r9
Mechanism: r3 is r9's ONLY backbone neighbor (r9's other
  interface is a stub LAN). r9 owns the 19.0.0.0/8 and
  90.0.0.0/8 prefixes. With the link down, the adjacency
  drops and r9 is fully isolated -- its prefixes disappear
  from the backbone RIBs.
Localization: r3 (eth toward r9)
Root cause: backbone link r3<->r9 is down
Fix: bring the link back up

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on r3's eth0 interface, which connects to segment J — the only
physical link between r3 and r9. During the maintenance window, r3's eth0
was brought administratively down (kernel flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST>
with no UP or LOWER_UP bits set, confirmed by `ip link show eth0`). The
interface still has its IP address (39.1.1.1/8) configured, and r3's FRR
running-config correctly includes `network 39.0.0.0/8 area 0`, but because
the interface is operationally down, OSPF cannot activate on it — FRR
reports "eth0 is down / OSPF not enabled on this interface."

As a result, r3 holds zero OSPF neighbors on eth0 and cannot form an
adjacency with r9. r9 is the sole originator of the three affected prefixes:
39.0.0.0/8 (directly connected on r9 eth0), 90.0.0.0/8 (directly connected
on r9 eth1/segment CC), and the 19.x.x.x loopback ranges. With the r3↔r9
adjacency down, those LSAs never reach the rest of the OSPF domain, so they
vanish from r1's RIB — precisely matching the reported instability for
19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, and 90.0.0.0/8. r9's side of the link (eth0,
39.1.1.2/8) is fully UP; the break is one-sided on r3.

Root cause: r3's eth0 was left in a DOWN state after the maintenance window,
severing the only OSPF path to r9.

Corrective fix: On r3, run `ip link set eth0 up`. Once the interface is UP,
FRR will detect carrier, bring OSPF up on eth0, re-form the Full adjacency
with r9 (39.1.1.2), and flood r9's LSAs back into the domain — restoring
19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, and 90.0.0.0/8 in r1's RIB within one dead-interval.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly names r3's eth0 as the sole physical link to r9 (39.1.1.2) and attributes the failure to the r3<->r9 link being down.
The report explicitly states r9's prefixes (19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, 90.0.0.0/8) are lost from the backbone/RIB when the r3–r9 adjacency drops.
Recommends bringing r3's eth0 up (ip link set eth0 up), which will restore carrier, OSPF adjacency to r9 and re-flood the missing LSAs — matches the expected fix.

The log contains concrete observations (r3 eth0 state DOWN, r9 eth0 UP, r3's OSPF interface showing 'eth0 is down', and r1's RIB missing the prefixes per agent notes) that support the agent's conclusion that the r3–r9 link is the failure point; the inferred causal chain (down interface → adjacency lost → prefixes vanish) is logical and the investigation covers the necessary checks and remedy. Minor truncations leave a bit of evidence implicit (exact origin of all prefixes and full neighbor lists), but the conclusion is well justified by the recorded outputs.
